content:
Subscribing to the mailing list does not appear to work for me, I'm not getting any response back. I sent two mails to rust-for-linux+subscribe@vger.kernel.org, one without any mention, one with subscribe in the subject and a short body message. Checking the mail server log reveals: "delivery 107166: success: 44.238.234.78 accepted message. Remote host said: 250 2.0.0 Ok: queued as 0B626606A31C" and before that "as 5AD24606A31C", but no connection attempt back.

So either vger.kernel.org treats my mail as spam or something is broken. (I have just verified via http://multirbl.valli.org (via option of sending an actual email) that my outgoing mail server is not on blacklists (uribl.com shows but seems broken, their own checker has me not listed); I also haven't had delivery problems for a while.)
Did you make sure to send a plain text message without html?
Subscribing to the lists may not be the best way to consume them. There is tooling such as korgalore and lei that may work better for you.

Andreas Hindborg said:

Did you make sure to send a plain text message without html?

Yes. Here's the exact second message as passed to sendmail -t:

Return-Path: <ch@christianjaeger.ch>
MIME-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain;
 charset=utf-8
Content-Transfer-Encoding: 8bit
Subject: subscribe
From: Christian Jaeger <ch@christianjaeger.ch>
To: rust-for-linux+subscribe@vger.kernel.org
Message-ID: <nyy768pnr7hintpnxj3-1794562354@christianjaeger.ch>

Hi

Please subscribe me to the rust-for-linux mailing list.

Christian.

Andreas Hindborg said:

Subscribing to the lists may not be the best way to consume them. There is tooling such as korgalore and lei that may work better for you.

Good to know. But I'm currently primarily planning to follow discussions and I like reading threads in a mail client better than in the online archive, and that's not something those tools seem to help with.
(I noticed claimed NNTP support and might try this.)
(But then that might be unidirectional?)
lei allows you to define a filter and subscribe to that filter. It will output the emails in a maildir. You can then use your favorite tooling to consume that maildir.
I'm quite certain the filter can be for instance an email address.
I think korgalore is similar, but instead of local maildir output, it can dump the output at your email provider via imap.
I sent a message to the help desk about it.
Thanks to both of you. I'll check lei (but it might also be nicest if it just works "normally" :), I'll see what comes out of it.

PS. my mail server doesn't support SMTP encryption, that's the only thing I can otherwise think of (I've never had issues receiving mail except one other time from a newsletter delivery service (that I didn't learn about why it failed), I wonder whether that might be an issue nowadays).
(Also, I have over 150 local folders with current and past mailing list subscriptions, 21 currently active ones, and have never before had an issue with mailing lists.)

I just got the "Confirm subscription to rust-for-linux@vger.kernel.org" mail and have replied with the confirmation 2 minutes ago (still no "you're now subscribed" mail, ,aybe it just takes over an hour to react?).

And a few minutes ago, the "Confirm subscription to rust-for-linux@vger.kernel.org" has come in, 1h24 after vger.kernel.org accepted my confirmation.

Between my original subscription request and the "Confirm subscription to rust-for-linux@vger.kernel.org" mail 140 minutes had passed.

So it appears that it maybe just takes about 80-140 minutes for vger.kernel.org to react? I've never seen such a slow delivery but I guess that server may be really busy currently?

BTW in the mean time I've double checked the logs of my smtp server and have confirmed that every single connection attempt is accounted for, and there really was none other than the ones I got the two email above for that could have accounted for this mailing list (for e.g. greylisting attempts or other issues); so it's really vger.kernel.org being slow and not my server refusing any attempt.
Any chance this is related to Outlook outage?
(I'm not using Outlook (my server is qmail and a wrapper and qpsmtpd).)

Gary Guo said:

Any chance this is related to Outlook outage?

It's tangentially related to the Outlook outage yesterday -- this pushed all of our mail queues really high. We had over 1,000,000 messages sitting in the queue, largely waiting on outlook (plus the usual gmail, yahoo, proton). I've finally had enough and moved these providers into their own queue, so whenever they have an outage or throw a tantrum about us sending them a lot of mail, they don't affect everyone else's deliveries. The queues are finally draining and I expect we'll be back to quick deliveries in the next couple of hours.
Nice, thanks!
